old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-nwjl","title":"slot-claim signature covers only ordinal/IID/superframe_id; slots array forgeable; no claim_seq replay gate or expiry","description":"coap_slot_coord.c:316-337 reconstructs the signed message as SLOT_CLAIM:%02X:%IID:%08X from ordinal, gateway_iid, superframe_id only — NOT the slots array. GCP-6.5 (spec/08:117-160) mandates COSE_Sign1 over the full claim payload including slots/expiry/claim_seq. An adversary who captures one legitimate claim can re-attach the identical signature to a different slots array (same ordinal/IID/superframe_id): schnorr48_verify passes and process_claim registers attacker-chosen slots under the victim IID, with lowest-IID conflict resolution favoring the forgery (airtime hijack / scheduling DoS attributed to a legit gateway). Also missing per spec GCP-6.5 step 7 (expiry \u003e now check; struct lichen_slot_claim has no expiry field) and step 8 + claim_seq persistence table (MUST reject claim_seq \u003c= cached; no claim_seq field or replay cache). Fix: sign the canonical CBOR encoding of the whole claim (or implement the COSE_Sign1 envelope), add expiry + NV-persisted claim_seq; align response codes while touching (spec step 10 says 2.04 Changed, impl returns 2.01; step 11 says 4.09 with winning gateway's claim, impl sends NULL payload). Design with the sibling bead (decoder cannot carry signatures).","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-08-28T17:14:21.55613Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-08-28T17:14:21.55613Z"}
